sentences.zh: 建元四年，高帝山陵，昭皇后應遷祔。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 4: the High Emperor's imperial tomb was completed; Empress Zhao was to be moved for collateral enshrinement.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 4 the High Emperor's tomb was finished and Empress Zhao was due to be transferred for collateral enshrinement.

sentences.zh: 祠部疑有祖祭及遣啟諸奠九飯之儀不？

translations.literal: The Sacrificial Affairs bureau questioned whether there should be ancestral sacrifice and the rites of dispatching the opening presentation, the various presentation offerings, and the nine servings of food.
translations.idiomatic: The Sacrificial Affairs bureau asked whether ancestral sacrifice was required, and whether the rites for dispatching the opening presentation, presentation offerings, and nine food servings applied.

sentences.zh: 左僕射王儉議：「奠如大斂。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「Presentation offerings should follow the model of the greater encoffinment.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「Presentation offerings should be handled like the greater encoffinment.

sentences.zh: 賀循云『從墓之墓皆設奠，如將葬廟朝之禮』。

translations.literal: He Xun said 『When moving from tomb to tomb, presentation offerings are always set out, as with the rites of the temple audience before burial.』
translations.idiomatic: He Xun said 『Whenever the grave is moved, offerings are set out, as when the coffin is about to be buried and the court pays temple audience.』

sentences.zh: 范寧云『將窆而奠』。

translations.literal: Fan Ning said 『Presentation offerings are made when the coffin is about to be lowered.』
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ning said 『Offerings are made when the coffin is about to be interred.』

sentences.zh: 雖不稱為祖，而不得無祭。

translations.literal: Though it is not called ancestral sacrifice, sacrifice cannot be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one does not call it ancestral sacrifice, an offering cannot be omitted.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」The court adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 有司又奏：「昭皇后神主在廟，今遷祔葬，

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized again: 「The spirit tablet of Empress Zhao is in the temple; now, for the move and collateral enshrinement burial,
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices submitted again: 「Empress Zhao's spirit tablet is already in the temple; for the transfer and collateral enshrinement burial,

translations.literal: Collation: the received text reads 廣; 廟 is adopted below.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: received 廣, emended to 廟.

sentences.zh: 〔廟〕有虞以安神，神既已處廟，改葬出靈，豈應虞祭？

translations.literal: 〔廟〕the temple holds the yu rite to settle the spirit; since the spirit is already lodged in the temple, to reinter and remove the soul-seat—should a yu sacrifice still be performed?
translations.idiomatic: At the temple the yu rite settles the spirit. The spirit is already in the temple; if one reinterrs and removes the soul-seat, should there still be a yu sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 鄭注改葬云『從廟之廟，禮宜同從墓之墓』。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary on reburial says 『When moving from temple to temple, ritual propriety should match moving from tomb to tomb.』
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's note on reburial says 『Moving from temple to temple should follow the same rule as moving from grave to grave.』

sentences.zh: 事何容異！

translations.literal: How could the affair be treated differently!
translations.idiomatic: How could the cases differ!

sentences.zh: 前代謂應無虞。

translations.literal: Earlier ages held that there should be no yu rite.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier practice held that no yu rite was required.

sentences.zh: 」左僕射王儉議：「范寧云『葬必有魂車』。

translations.literal: 」Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「Fan Ning said 『Burial must have a soul cart.』
translations.idiomatic: 」Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「Fan Ning said 『Every burial requires a soul cart.』

sentences.zh: 若不為其歸，神將安舍？

translations.literal: If one does not provide for its return, where will the spirit lodge?
translations.idiomatic: If you do not receive it home, where will the spirit rest?

sentences.zh: 世中改葬，即墓所施靈設祭，何得不祭而毀耶？

translations.literal: In this age, when graves are moved, a soul-seat is set up at the tomb and sacrifices are performed—how can one offer no sacrifice and yet destroy the seat?
translations.idiomatic: When graves are moved in our time, a soul-seat is installed at the tomb and offerings are made—how can one destroy the seat without sacrificing?

sentences.zh: 賀循云『既窆，設奠於墓，以終其事』。

translations.literal: He Xun said 『Once the coffin is lowered, set presentation offerings at the grave to complete the affair.』
translations.idiomatic: He Xun said 『After interment, set offerings at the grave to finish the rite.』

sentences.zh: 雖非正虞，亦粗相似。

translations.literal: Though it is not a proper yu rite, it is roughly similar.
translations.idiomatic: It is not a full yu rite, but it is close enough.

sentences.zh: 晉氏脩復五陵，宋朝敬后改葬，皆有虞。

translations.literal: When Jin restored the five imperial tombs, and when Song reinterred Empress Jing, both had yu rites.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's restoration of the five imperial tombs and Song's reburial of Empress Jing both included yu rites.

sentences.zh: 今設虞非疑。

translations.literal: To set up a yu rite now is not in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: There is no question that a yu rite should be held now.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」The court adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，皇太子妃薨，前宮臣疑所服。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 2: the crown prince's consort died; former palace officers questioned what mourning garb to wear.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 2 the crown prince's consort died, and former palace staff disputed the mourning they should wear.

sentences.zh: 左僕射王儉議：「禮記文王世子『父在斯為子，君在斯為臣』。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「The Book of Rites, King Wen as Crown Prince, says 『While the father lives one is a son; while the lord lives one is a subject.』
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「The Book of Rites, King Wen as Crown Prince, says 『While the father lives you are a son; while the ruler lives you are a subject.』

sentences.zh: 且漢魏以來，宮僚充備，臣隸之節，具體在三。

translations.literal: Moreover, from Han and Wei onward palace staff have been fully appointed; the protocol of subject and servant is complete in all three bonds.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei on, palace offices have been fully staffed; the duties of subject and servant are complete in every bond.

sentences.zh: 昔庾翼妻喪，王允、滕弘謂府吏宜有小君之服，況臣節之重邪？

translations.literal: When Yu Yi's wife died, Wang Yun and Teng Hong held that prefectural clerks should wear mourning for the lesser lady—how much more when the weight of subjecthood is at stake?
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yi's wife died, Wang Yun and Teng Hong said prefectural clerks should mourn the master's wife; how much more when the bond of subjecthood is in question?

sentences.zh: 宜依禮為舊君妻齊衰三月，居官之身，竝合屬假，朝晡臨哭，悉繫東宮。

translations.literal: They should follow ritual and wear three months' second-degree mourning for a former lord's wife; those in office should all be granted leave, attend morning and evening wailing at the Eastern Palace, and keep to that quarter entirely.
translations.idiomatic: They should observe three months' second-degree mourning for a former lord's wife. All who hold office should receive leave, wail morning and evening at the Eastern Palace, and remain attached to that quarter.

sentences.zh: 今臣之未從官在遠者，於居官之所，屬寧二日半，仍行喪成服，遣牋表，不得奔赴。

translations.literal: As for officers not yet in post who are far away, at the place where they hold office they should observe two and a half days of leave for rest, then complete the mourning garb, send a written report, and not rush to attend in person.
translations.idiomatic: Officers not yet in post who are distant should, at their place of service, take two and a half days' leave for rest, then complete mourning dress, send a memorial, and not travel to attend in person.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」The court adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 太子妃斬草乘黃，議建銘旌。

translations.literal: When the crown prince's consort cut the mourning staff and rode the yellow carriage, there was debate over erecting the name pennant.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince's consort cut the mourning staff and took the yellow carriage, officials debated whether to raise the name pennant.

sentences.zh: 僕射王儉議：「禮，既塗棺，祝取銘置于殯東，大斂畢，便應建于西階之東。」

translations.literal: Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「Ritual says: once the coffin is coated, the invoker takes the inscription and places it east of the bier; when the greater encoffinment is complete, it should at once be set up east of the western steps.」
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「Ritual requires that once the coffin is sealed, the invoker places the inscription east of the bier; when the greater encoffinment is finished, the pennant should be raised east of the western steps.」

sentences.zh: 宋大明二年，太子妃薨，建九旒。

translations.literal: In Song, Daming year 2, when a crown prince's consort died, nine tassels were erected.
translations.idiomatic: In Song Daming 2, when a crown prince's consort died, a nine-tassel canopy was used.

sentences.zh: 有司又議：「斬草日建旒與不？

translations.literal: The relevant offices debated again: 「On the day of cutting the mourning staff, should tassels be erected or not?
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices debated again: 「On the day the mourning staff is cut, should tassels be erected?

sentences.zh: 若建旒，應幾旒？

translations.literal: If tassels are erected, how many tassels should there be?
translations.idiomatic: If they are, how many tassels?

sentences.zh: 及畫龍升降云何？

translations.literal: And how should the painted dragon ascend and descend?
translations.idiomatic: And how should the painted dragon rise and fall?

sentences.zh: 又用幾翣？

translations.literal: And how many feather screens should be used?
translations.idiomatic: And how many feather screens?

sentences.zh: 」僕射王儉議：「旒本是命服，無關於凶事，今公卿以下，平存不能備禮，故在凶乃建耳。

translations.literal: 」Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「Tassels are originally insignia of conferred rank and have no bearing on inauspicious affairs; today, from the highest ministers down, in ordinary times they cannot fully observe ritual, so only in mourning are tassels erected.
translations.idiomatic: 」Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「Tassels belong to insignia of rank, not to mourning; today even the highest ministers cannot keep full ritual in normal times, so tassels are raised only in mourning.

sentences.zh: 東宮秩同上公九命之儀，妃與儲君一體，義不容異，無緣未同常例，別立凶旒。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace's rank follows the nine-rank protocol of a lord equal to the Three Dukes; the consort and the heir are one body—in principle they cannot differ. There is no reason to depart from the usual rule and set up a separate mourning tassel.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace ranks with a lord of ninefold dignity, like the Three Dukes; consort and heir are one—by right they cannot differ. There is no ground to break from ordinary usage and invent a special mourning tassel.

sentences.zh: 大明舊事，是不經詳議，率爾便行耳。

translations.literal: The Daming precedent was not the product of careful deliberation; it was carried out hastily.
translations.idiomatic: The Daming precedent was never fully debated; it was done in haste.

sentences.zh: 今宜考以禮典，不得効尤從失。

translations.literal: Now one should consult the ritual canon and not follow a bad example into error.
translations.idiomatic: The canon should govern now, not a faulty precedent copied again.

sentences.zh: 吉部伍自有桁輅，凶部別有銘旌，若復立旒，復置何處？

translations.literal: The auspicious train already has its framed carriage; the mourning train has its own name pennant—if tassels are erected again, where would they be placed?
translations.idiomatic: The auspicious procession already has its framed carriage; the mourning train has its name pennant—if tassels are added, where would they go?

sentences.zh: 翣自用八。

translations.literal: Eight feather screens should be used.
translations.idiomatic: Use eight feather screens.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」The court adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「大明故事，太子妃玄宮中有石誌。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: 「By Daming precedent, crown princes' consorts had stone epitaphs in the inner tomb chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices submitted: 「Under Daming precedent, crown princes' consorts had stone epitaphs in the inner tomb chamber.

sentences.zh: 參議墓銘不出禮典。

translations.literal: Deliberation shows that tomb inscriptions are not in the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, tomb inscriptions are not prescribed in the ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 近宋元嘉中，顏延作王球石誌。

translations.literal: Recently, in Song's Yuanjia era, Yan Yan composed a stone epitaph for Wang Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, in Song's Yuanjia reign, Yan Yan wrote a stone epitaph for Wang Qiu.

sentences.zh: 素族無碑策，故以紀德。

translations.literal: Plain clans had no steles or written encomia, so the stone was used to record virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Humble families had no steles or written encomia, so stone was used to record their merit.

sentences.zh: 自爾以來，王公以下，咸共遵用。

translations.literal: From that time on, princes and dukes downward all followed it in common practice.
translations.idiomatic: After that, everyone from princes and dukes down observed it alike.

sentences.zh: 儲妃之重，禮殊恆列，既有哀策，謂不須石誌。

translations.literal: The weight of a crown prince's consort makes her ritual distinct from the ordinary ranks; since there is already an elegiac decree, they held a stone epitaph unnecessary.
translations.idiomatic: A crown prince's consort outranks ordinary wives; with an elegiac decree already issued, a stone epitaph was deemed unnecessary.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」The court adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「穆妃卒哭後，靈還在道，遇朔望，當須設祭不？

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: 「After Consort Mu's zui ku, the spirit-seat was still on the road; on new- and full-moon days, should offerings be set out or not?
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices submitted: 「After Consort Mu completed the end of wailing, the spirit journey was still underway; should new- and full-moon offerings be held?

sentences.zh: 」王儉議：「既虞卒哭，祭之於廟，本是祭序昭穆耳，未全同卒吉四時之祭也，所以有朔望殷事。

translations.literal: 」Wang Jian argued: 「After the yu and zui ku, sacrifice in the ancestral temple is only fixing the order of zhao and mu; it is not wholly the same as the four seasonal sacrifices when mourning is fully ended, which is why there are elaborate new- and full-moon rites.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wang Jian replied: 「After yu and zui ku, temple sacrifice only sets zhao-mu order; it is not the same as the four seasonal rites after mourning ends—hence the elaborate new- and full-moon observances.

sentences.zh: 蕃國不行權制，宋江夏王妃卒哭以後，朔望設祭。

translations.literal: Feudatory states do not follow expedient regulations; under Song, after the Princess of Jiangxia finished zui ku, they set out offerings on new and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal kingdoms did not follow the crown's expedients; in Song, the Jiangxia princess continued new- and full-moon offerings after zui ku.

sentences.zh: 帝室既以卒哭除喪，無緣方有朔望之祭。

translations.literal: The imperial house, having removed mourning at zui ku, has no reason then to hold new- and full-moon sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial line ends mourning at zui ku; there is no ground for new- and full-moon rites afterward.

sentences.zh: 靈筵雖未升廟堂，而舫中即成行廟，猶如桓玄及宋高祖長沙、臨川二國，竝有移廟之禮。

translations.literal: Though the spirit-seat had not yet ascended to the temple hall, on the boat it already formed a traveling temple, as when Huan Xuan and under Song Gaozu the states of Changsha and Linchuan both had the rite of moving the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Though the spirit-seat had not reached the temple, the barge itself served as a traveling shrine—as with Huan Xuan and, under Song Gaozu, the Changsha and Linchuan domains, which all observed temple-transfer rites.

sentences.zh: 豈復謂靈筵在途，便設殷事耶？

translations.literal: How could one say that because the spirit-seat is on the road, one should set up elaborate rites?
translations.idiomatic: Surely one does not hold elaborate new- and full-moon rites merely because the spirit-seat is still en route?

sentences.zh: 推此而言，朔望不復俟祭。

translations.literal: Pushing this reasoning further, one need not wait for new and full moon to sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On that reasoning, new- and full-moon offerings need not be observed.

sentences.zh: 宋懿后時舊事不及此，益可知時議。

translations.literal: Former practice under Empress Yi of Song did not reach this point, which further shows the opinion of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song's Empress Yi the old precedent did not go so far, which shows what contemporaries thought.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」The court adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 建元三年，有司奏：「皇太子穆妃以去年七月薨，其年閏九月。

translations.literal: Jianyuan year 3, the relevant offices memorialized: 「The crown prince's Consort Mu died last seventh month; that year had an intercalary ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 3 the relevant offices submitted: 「Crown Prince Consort Mu died last July; the year also had an intercalary ninth month.

sentences.zh: 未審當月數閏？

translations.literal: Should the intercalary month be counted in the month-tally?
translations.idiomatic: Should the intercalary month count toward the month tally?

sentences.zh: 為應以閏附正月？

translations.literal: Or should the intercalary be attached to the first month?
translations.idiomatic: Or should it be folded into the first month?

sentences.zh: 若用月數數閏者，南郡王兄弟便應以此四月晦小祥，至於祥月，不為有疑不？

translations.literal: If one counts months and counts the intercalary, the Prince of Nanjun's brothers should observe xiaoxiang on the last day of this fourth month; as for the month of xiang—is there any doubt?
translations.idiomatic: If months are counted and the intercalary is included, the Nanjun princes should hold xiaoxiang on the last day of the fourth month—would that leave the xiang month in doubt?

sentences.zh: 」左僕射王儉議：「三百六旬，尚書明義，文公納幣，春秋致譏。

translations.literal: 」Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「Three hundred and sixty days—the Documents make the meaning plain; Duke Wen's betrothal gifts drew the Spring and Autumn Annals' rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: 」Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: 「Three hundred and sixty days—the Documents state it plainly; Duke Wen's betrothal gifts drew the Spring and Autumn Annals' rebuke.

sentences.zh: 穀梁云『積分而成月』。

translations.literal: Guliang said 『Months are formed by accumulated fractions.』
translations.idiomatic: Guliang said: 『Months form from accumulated fractional days.』

sentences.zh: 公羊云『天無是月』。

translations.literal: Gongyang said 『Heaven has no such month.』
translations.idiomatic: Gongyang said: 『Heaven has no intercalary month as such.』

sentences.zh: 雖然，左氏謂告朔為得禮。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, Zuoshi holds that announcing the new moon is proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the Zuo tradition treats announcing the new moon as ritually correct.

sentences.zh: 是故先儒咸謂三年朞喪，歲數沒閏，大功以下，月數數閏。

translations.literal: Therefore the early Ru all say that for the three-year term mourning, years absorb the intercalary month, while for lesser grades one counts months and counts the intercalary.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ru thus held: three-year term mourning counts by years and absorbs the intercalary; for lesser grades, count months and include the intercalary.

sentences.zh: 夫閏者，蓋是年之餘日，而月之異朔，所以吳商云『含閏以正朞，允協情理』。

translations.literal: Intercalary, in general, is the year's surplus days and the month's variant new moon; hence Wu Shang said 『Include the intercalary to correct the term—it truly fits reason.』
translations.idiomatic: An intercalary month is surplus days in a year and an extra reckoning in the month; Wu Shang said: 『Wrap the intercalary into the term—that best fits reason.』

sentences.zh: 今杖朞之喪，雖以十〔一〕月而小祥，至於祥縞，必須周歲。

translations.literal: For staff-and-term mourning today, though xiaoxiang comes in the eleventh month (received text: ten [one]), for xiang and hemp mourning a full year is required.
translations.idiomatic: For staff-and-one-year mourning, xiaoxiang may fall in the eleventh month, but xiang and hemp mourning require a full cycle of the year.

sentences.zh: 凡厭屈之禮，要取象正服。

translations.literal: In all compressed mourning rites, the key is to mirror the normal garment stages.
translations.idiomatic: Compressed mourning mirrors the normal garment stages.

sentences.zh: 祥縞相去二月，厭降小祥，亦以則之。

translations.literal: Xiang and hemp mourning are two months apart; compressing xiaoxiang follows the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang and hemp are two months apart; compressed xiaoxiang follows that spacing.

sentences.zh: 又且求之名義，則小祥本以年限，考於倫例，則相去必應二朔。

translations.literal: Moreover, by its name and meaning xiaoxiang is fundamentally by yearly limit; checked against parallel cases, the interval must be two new moons.
translations.idiomatic: By name, xiaoxiang is reckoned by years; by parallel cases, two new moons must separate the stages.

sentences.zh: 今以厭屈而先祥，不得謂此事之非朞，事既同條，情無異貫，沒閏之理，固在言先。

translations.literal: Now, because mourning is compressed the xiang comes early; one cannot say this is not term mourning—the matter falls under the same rubric, the feeling is not different in kind, and the logic of absorbing the intercalary is already stated above.
translations.idiomatic: Compression moves xiang earlier, but the case is still term mourning under the same rule and feeling; absorbing the intercalary was already argued.

sentences.zh: 設令祥在此晦，則去縞三月，依附准例，益復為礙。

translations.literal: Suppose xiang fell on this month's last day; then only three months to hemp—by precedent that would again be obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: If xiang fell on this month's last day, hemp would be only three months away—again at odds with precedent.

sentences.zh: 謂應須五月晦乃祥。

translations.literal: They held that xiang should be on the last day of the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang should fall on the last day of the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 此國之大典，宜共精詳。

translations.literal: This is a great statute of the state and should be examined together in detail.
translations.idiomatic: This is a state ritual of the first order and deserves joint, careful review.

sentences.zh: 並通關八座丞郎，研盡同異。」

translations.literal: It should be circulated to the Eight Seats, aides, and directors for thorough study of agreement and difference.」
translations.idiomatic: Circulate it to the Eight Seats, aides, and directors to settle every point of agreement and difference.」

sentences.zh: 尚書令褚淵難儉議曰：「厭屈之典，由所尊奪情，故祥縞備制，而年月不申。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Chu Yuan objected to Jian's argument: 「The statute of compressed mourning exists because respect for the honored curtails grief, so xiang and hemp keep full form while years and months are not fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: Director Chu Yuan objected to Jian: 「Compressed mourning exists because respect for the honored curtails grief, so xiang and hemp keep full form while years and months are not fully expressed.

sentences.zh: 今以十一月而祥，從朞可知。

translations.literal: Now to hold xiang in the eleventh month shows it follows the term.
translations.idiomatic: Holding xiang in the eleventh month already shows term reckoning.

sentences.zh: 既計以月數，則應數閏以成典。

translations.literal: Since one reckons by months, one should count the intercalary to complete the statute.
translations.idiomatic: If reckoning is by months, the intercalary should be counted to complete the rule.

sentences.zh: 若猶含之，何以異於縞制。

translations.literal: If one still absorbs it, how does that differ from the hemp-mourning rule?
translations.idiomatic: If the intercalary is still absorbed, how is that different from hemp mourning?

sentences.zh: 疑者正以祥之當閏，月數相縣。

translations.literal: Doubters precisely because xiang should fall in an intercalary month, and month-counts are far apart.
translations.idiomatic: The doubt is precisely that xiang should coincide with an intercalary month while month-counts stand apart.

sentences.zh: 積分餘閏，曆象所弘。

translations.literal: Accumulating fractional days and surplus intercalary is what the calendar promotes.
translations.idiomatic: Fractional days and surplus intercalary are what calendrical science upholds.

sentences.zh: 計月者數閏，故有餘月，計年者苞含，故致盈積。

translations.literal: Those who count months count the intercalary, hence leftover months; those who count years encompass, hence surplus accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Month-reckoning counts the intercalary and leaves extra months; year-reckoning encompasses and yields surplus.

sentences.zh: 稱理從制，有何不可？」

translations.literal: To follow statute as reason dictates—what could be wrong?」
translations.idiomatic: If reason and statute align, what objection remains?」

sentences.zh: 儉又荅淵難曰：「含閏之義，通儒所難。

translations.literal: Jian again answered Yuan's objection: 「The meaning of including the intercalary—even comprehensive Ru find it hard.
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered Yuan again: 「The meaning of including the intercalary—even leading Ru find it hard.

sentences.zh: 但祥本應朞，屈而不遂。

translations.literal: Yet xiang originally should fall at the term and was bent short of completion.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang should come at term's end but was bent short.

sentences.zh: 語事則名體具存，論哀則情無以異。

translations.literal: In speaking of the matter, names and forms are fully preserved; in speaking of grief, feeling is not different.
translations.idiomatic: In form the names and stages remain; in grief the feeling is unchanged.

sentences.zh: 迹雖數月，義實計年，閏是年之歸餘，故宜總而苞之。

translations.literal: The trace is months, but the meaning is truly years; the intercalary is the year's remainder and should be gathered and encompassed.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar shows months, but the meaning is years; the intercalary is the year's remainder and should be wrapped into the whole.

sentences.zh: 朞而兩祥，緣尊故屈，祥則沒閏，象年所申，屈申兼著，二途具舉。

translations.literal: Term and two xiang—because of respect, compression; at xiang, absorb intercalary, expressing the year—compression and expression both shown, both paths set forth.
translations.idiomatic: One term, two xiang: respect compresses; at xiang the intercalary is absorbed to express the year—compression and full expression both appear, both paths named.

sentences.zh: 經記之旨，其在茲乎！

translations.literal: The point of the classics and records—is it not here!
translations.idiomatic: Is this not the thrust of the classics?

sentences.zh: 如使五月小祥，六月乃閏，則祥之去縞，事成二月，是為十一月以象前朞，二朔以放後歲，名有區域，不得相參。

translations.literal: If xiaoxiang came in the fifth month and the sixth were intercalary, then from xiang to hemp would be only two months—that would use the eleventh month to mirror the prior term and two new moons to discharge the later year; names have separate domains and cannot be mixed.
translations.idiomatic: If xiaoxiang fell in the fifth month and the sixth were intercalary, only two months would remain to hemp—making the eleventh month stand for the prior term and two new moons discharge the later year; the categories differ and cannot be combined.

sentences.zh: 魯襄二十八年『十二月乙未，楚子卒』。

translations.literal: Lu Xiang year 28: 『Twelfth month, day yiwei, the Chu ruler died.』
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiang year 28: 『In the twelfth month, on yiwei, the Chu ruler died.』

sentences.zh: 唯書上月，初不言閏，此又附上之明義也。

translations.literal: It records only the upper month and at first does not speak of intercalary—this again is clear meaning attached to the upper month.
translations.idiomatic: It names only the recorded month and never the intercalary—a clear rule for how the upper month is written.

sentences.zh: 鄭、射、王、賀唯云朞則沒閏，初不復區別杖朞之中祥，將謂不俟言矣。

translations.literal: Zheng, She, Wang, and He only said that at the term one absorbs the intercalary; they did not further distinguish xiang within staff-term mourning—one may suppose it goes without saying.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, She, Wang, and He said only that term mourning absorbs the intercalary; they did not separate xiang within staff-and-term mourning—that surely needs no argument.

sentences.zh: 成休甫云『大祥後禫，有閏別數之』。

translations.literal: Cheng Xiufu said 『After da xiang, yong and sacrificial service—if there is intercalary, count it separately.』
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xiufu said: 『After great xiang, yong and the offering rites count the intercalary separately.』

sentences.zh: 明杖朞之祥，不得方於綅縞之末。

translations.literal: The clear xiang of staff-period mourning cannot be equated with the end of sackcloth-and-hemp.
translations.idiomatic: The minor felicity of staff-period mourning cannot be measured against the tail of coarse hemp and sackcloth.

sentences.zh: 即恩如彼，就例如此。

translations.literal: As the grace there was such, so by precedent it is thus.
translations.idiomatic: If favor worked that way, precedent should work the same.

sentences.zh: 」淵又據舊義難儉十餘問，儉隨事解釋。

translations.literal: 」Yuan again raised more than ten objections from old interpretations against Jian; Jian answered each point as it arose.
translations.idiomatic: 」Chu Yuan pressed on with a dozen more objections drawn from older commentators; Jian rebutted each in turn.

sentences.zh: 祠部郎中王珪之議，謂「喪以閏施，功衰以下小祥值閏，則略而不言。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices Wang Guizhi memorialized, saying 「When mourning is calculated with leap months, for merit-mourning and below, if minor felicity falls in a leap month it is passed over in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guizhi of the sacrifices bureau argued: 「Where mourning reckons leap months, for merit-mourning and lower grades a leap-month minor felicity is simply not named.

sentences.zh: 今雖厭〔屈〕，祥名猶存，異於餘服。

translations.literal: Now though compressed〔abbreviated〕, the name of xiang still remains, differing from other garments.
translations.idiomatic: Even when mourning is compressed, the term xiang still stands—unlike other grades of dress.

sentences.zh: 計月為數，屈追慕之心，以遠為邇。

translations.literal: Counting by months as the number compresses the heart of longing, making the distant near.
translations.idiomatic: To count by months is to shorten grief and pull what should be far back to what feels near.

sentences.zh: 日既餘分，月非正朔，含而全制，於情唯允。

translations.literal: Days are already surplus fractions; months are not proper new moons—embracing them to complete the rule is alone fitting to feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Leap days are the year's remainder; leap months are not true first days of the month—yet folding them in to finish the full mourning term is what feeling allows.

sentences.zh: 僕射儉議，理據詳博，謹所附同。

translations.literal: Vice Director Jian's proposal, with reasons detailed and broad—I respectfully attach myself to agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wang Jian's argument is thorough; I respectfully concur.

sentences.zh: 今司徒淵始雖疑難，再經往反，未同儉議。

translations.literal: Now Minister of Works Yuan at first doubted and objected; after two rounds of exchange he still does not agree with Jian's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Chu Yuan first objected; after two exchanges he still did not accept Jian's view.

sentences.zh: 依舊八座丞郎通共博議為允。

translations.literal: According to old precedent, the eight excellencies and directors and aides should jointly debate to find what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom the eight excellencies and all directors and aides should debate the matter together and settle what is right.

sentences.zh: 以來五月晦小祥，其祥禫自依常限。

translations.literal: From now on, minor felicity on the last day of the fifth month; xiang and chan themselves follow the usual limits.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth minor felicity on the last day of the fifth month; xiang and chan thereafter on the ordinary schedule.

sentences.zh: 奏御，班下內外。

translations.literal: Memorial presented to the throne; promulgated within and without.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went up; the decision was issued court and realm.

translations.literal: 」An edict said 「Approved.」
translations.idiomatic: 」The edict read: 「Approved.」

sentences.zh: 皇太子穆妃服，尚書左丞兼著作郎王逡問左僕射王儉：「中軍南郡王小祥，應待聞喜不？

translations.literal: For mourning the crown prince's Consort Mu, Left Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Director of Composition Wang Xun asked Left Vice Director Wang Jian: 「The Central Army, the Prince of Nan Commandery—on minor felicity, should he wait for Wenxi or not?
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for the crown prince's Consort Mu, Wang Xun—left director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent director of composition—asked Vice Director Wang Jian: 「For the Central Army prince of Nan Commandery, should minor felicity wait on Wenxi?

sentences.zh: 穆妃七月二十四日薨，聞喜公八月發哀，計十一月之限，應在六月。

translations.literal: Consort Mu died on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month; the Duke of Wenxi began mourning in the eighth month; reckoning the eleventh-month limit, it should fall in the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Mu died on the twenty-fourth of the seventh month; the duke of Wenxi began mourning in the eighth; by an eleven-month count, minor felicity should land in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 南郡王為當同取六月，則大祥復申一月，應用八月，非復正月，在存親之義，若各自為祥，廬堊相閒，玄素雜糅，未審當有此疑不？

translations.literal: If the Prince of Nan Commandery is to take the same sixth month, then major felicity would again be extended one month and should fall in the eighth—not the first month again; in the meaning of cherishing kin, if each observes felicity on his own, thatched huts and plastered walls would alternate, black and white mixed together—has there ever been such a doubt?
translations.idiomatic: If the prince of Nan were to share the sixth month, major felicity would slip another month to the eighth—not back to the first month; and if each brother kept his own felicity schedule, thatched mourning huts and whitewashed walls would alternate, black and white interleaved—is that really in doubt?

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「送往有已，復生有節，罔極非服制所申，祥縞明示終之斷。

translations.literal: 」Jian said: 「Sending off the dead has its end; returning to life has its seasons; boundless grief is not what garment rules express—xiang and hemp mark the clear break of finality.
translations.idiomatic: 」Jian replied: 「The dead are sent off to their limit; the living return on fixed seasons. Boundless grief is not what the garment code is for—xiang and hemp mark where mourning ends.

sentences.zh: 相待之義，經記無聞。

translations.literal: The meaning of waiting for one another is nowhere heard in the classics and records.
translations.idiomatic: The classics and commentaries nowhere speak of waiting for one another.

sentences.zh: 世人多以廬室衰麻，不宜有異，故相去一二月者，或申以俱除。

translations.literal: People mostly hold that thatched rooms and hemp garments should not differ, so when dates fall one or two months apart they sometimes extend so as to remove mourning together.
translations.idiomatic: Most people think thatched huts and hemp dress ought not to differ, so when dates fall a month or two apart they sometimes stretch the schedule to end mourning together.

sentences.zh: 此所謂任情徑行，未達禮旨。

translations.literal: This is what is called following feeling and going straight—not reaching the aim of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: That is indulging private feeling, not grasping what ritual intends.

sentences.zh: 昔撰喪記，已嘗言之。

translations.literal: When I compiled the Mourning Record, I already spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: I said as much when I compiled the Mourning Record.

sentences.zh: 遠還之人，自有為而未祭，在家之子，立何辭以不變？

translations.literal: One who returns from afar may have duties yet unperformed in sacrifice; a son at home—on what grounds would he refuse to change garments?
translations.idiomatic: A man returning from afar may still owe rites he has not performed; a son at home—what excuse has he to keep old garments unchanged?

sentences.zh: 禮有除喪而歸者，此則經記之遺文，不待之明據。

translations.literal: Ritual has one who removes mourning and returns home—this is a surviving line in the classics and records, not something that awaits clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: The rites allow removing mourning garments on return—that is a surviving line in the classics, not something needing explicit proof.

sentences.zh: 假使應待，則相去彌年，亦宜必待，乃為衰絰永服以窮生，吉蠲長絕於宗廟，斯不可矣。

translations.literal: If one should wait, then even when separated by a full year one ought still to wait—then hemp would be worn to the end of life and auspicious purification long cut off from the ancestral temple; that cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: If waiting were required, even a year's gap would demand waiting—then one would wear hemp to the grave and cut off sacrifice at the ancestral temple forever; that is impossible.

sentences.zh: 苟曰非宜，則旬月之閒，亦不容申。

translations.literal: If it is said to be improper, then within the space of ten days or a month it also cannot be extended.
translations.idiomatic: If it is wrong in principle, it is wrong whether the gap is ten days or ten months.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 禮有倫序，義無徒設。

translations.literal: Ritual has order and sequence; the meaning does not stand alone without purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual has its order; meaning is never set up for nothing.

sentences.zh: 今遠則不待，近必相須，禮例既乖，即心無取。

translations.literal: Now the distant does not wait, yet the near must depend on one another—ritual precedent is already at odds, and the heart cannot accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Today the distant mourner need not wait, yet the near must—precedent is already twisted, and the heart will not follow.

sentences.zh: 若疑兄弟同居，吉凶舛雜，則古有異宮之義。

translations.literal: If the doubt is brothers dwelling together with auspicious and inauspicious mixed, antiquity had the principle of separate residences.
translations.idiomatic: If the worry is brothers under one roof with joy and mourning tangled, antiquity allowed separate households.

sentences.zh: 設無異宮，則遠還之子，自應開立別門，以終喪事。

translations.literal: If there is no separate residence, then the son returning from afar should himself open a separate gate and finish mourning there.
translations.idiomatic: Without separate residences, the son back from afar should set up his own gate and finish mourning apart.

sentences.zh: 靈筵祭奠，隨在家之人，再朞而毀。

translations.literal: Spirit mats and offerings follow whoever is at home; after two periods they are destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit mat and offerings stay with whoever remains at home and are dismantled after two mourning periods.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，奔喪禮云『為位不奠』，鄭玄云『以其精神不存乎此也』。

translations.literal: The reason is that Rites for Rush Mourning says 『Setting a place but not offering』, and Zheng Xuan says 『Because the spirit is not present here.』
translations.idiomatic: Rush-mourning rites say: 『One sets a place but does not offer』—Zheng Xuan: 『Because the spirit is not present there.』

sentences.zh: 聞哀不時，寔緣在遠。

translations.literal: Hearing of the bereavement not in season truly comes from being far away.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the news out of season is simply because one was far away.

sentences.zh: 為位不奠，益有可安。

translations.literal: Setting a place but not offering—all the more may one be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Setting a place without offering is all the more reason to be at ease about it.

sentences.zh: 此自有為而然，不關嫡庶。

translations.literal: This follows from having duties of one's own; it does not concern primary wife and concubine.
translations.idiomatic: That follows from one's own obligations; it has nothing to do with primary wife or concubine.

sentences.zh: 庶子在家，亦不待嫡矣。

translations.literal: A secondary son at home also does not wait for the primary heir.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary son at home does not wait on the heir either.

sentences.zh: 而況儲妃正體王室，中軍長嫡之重，天朝又行權制，進退彌復非疑。

translations.literal: How much more the crown prince's consort as the orthodox body of the royal house, the weight of the Central Army heir as eldest son, and the court moreover applying expedient rules—going forward or back is doubly beyond doubt.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the crown prince's consort is the orthodox wife of the house, the Central Army heir is the eldest son, and the court itself applies expedient mourning—there is no real doubt left.

sentences.zh: 謂不應相待。

translations.literal: I hold that they should not wait for one another.
translations.idiomatic: They should not wait on one another.

sentences.zh: 中軍祥縞之日，聞喜致哀而已，不受弔慰。

translations.literal: On the Central Army's day of xiang and hemp, Wenxi only begins mourning; he does not receive condolence visits.
translations.idiomatic: On the Central Army prince's xiang-and-hemp day, Wenxi begins mourning only—he does not receive callers.

sentences.zh: 及至忌辰變除，昆弟亦宜相就寫情而不對客。

translations.literal: When the anniversary of death arrives and garments change, brothers too should visit one another to pour out feeling but not receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: When the death anniversary comes and garments change, brothers may visit each other privately but should not receive guests.

sentences.zh: 此國之大典，宜通關八座丞郎，共盡同異，然〔後〕奏御。

translations.literal: This is a great statute of the state; it should be circulated to the eight excellencies and directors and aides to exhaust agreement and difference, then〔afterward〕 present to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: This is a great statute of the realm; it should go to the eight excellencies and all directors and aides for full debate, then be memorialized.

sentences.zh: 」司徒褚淵等二十人竝同儉議為允，請以為永制。

translations.literal: 」Minister of Works Chu Yuan and twenty others together agreed with Jian's proposal as fitting and asked that it be made permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: 」Minister of Works Chu Yuan and twenty colleagues endorsed Jian's view and asked that it be fixed as permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 詔「可」。

translations.literal: An edict said 「Approved.」
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: 「Approved.」

sentences.zh: 建元三年，太子穆妃薨，南郡王聞喜公國臣疑制君母服。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan, the crown prince's Consort Mu died; officials of the Prince of Nan Commandery and the Duke of Wenxi questioned mourning dress for a stepmother of the lord.
translations.idiomatic: Jianyuan 3: the crown prince's Consort Mu died; retainers of the prince of Nan Commandery and the duke of Wenxi disputed how to mourn a lord's stepmother.

sentences.zh: 儉又議：「禮『庶人為國君齊衰』，先儒云『庶人在官若府史之屬是也』。

translations.literal: Jian again memorialized: 「The rites say 『Commoners wear equated mourning for the lord of the state』, and early scholars say 『Commoners in office means clerks such as prefectural and commandery staff.』
translations.idiomatic: Jian argued again: 「The rites say 『Commoners in office wear equated mourning for the lord of the state』, and early scholars explain 『in office』 as clerks on a prince's or commandery staff.

sentences.zh: 又諸侯之大夫妻為夫人服繐衰七月，以此輕微疏遠，故不得盡禮。

translations.literal: Again, a great feudal lord's wife wears fine hemp for seven months for the lord's wife—because she is slight and distant, she cannot receive the full rite.
translations.idiomatic: A great feudal lord's wife wears fine hemp seven months for the lord's wife—being remote and slight in rank, she does not receive the full rite.

sentences.zh: 今皇孫自是蕃國之王公，太子穆妃是天朝之嫡婦。

translations.literal: Now the imperial grandson is himself a feudal king of a border state; the crown prince's Consort Mu is the orthodox daughter-in-law of the heavenly court.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson is a feudal king in his own domain; Consort Mu was the crown prince's orthodox wife in the heavenly court.

sentences.zh: 宮臣得申小君之禮，國官豈敢為夫人之敬。

translations.literal: Palace retainers may perform the rites due a lesser lady; how dare state officials perform the rites due a lady of the domain?
translations.idiomatic: Palace staff may perform rites for a lesser lady; domain officials dare not perform rites for a full lady of the house.

sentences.zh: 當單衣白帢素帶哭于中門外，每臨輒入，與宮官同。」

translations.literal: They should wear plain clothes, white headcloth, and plain belt and weep outside the middle gate; each time they attend they enter, the same as palace officers.」
translations.idiomatic: They should wear plain dress, white headcloth, and plain belt and weep outside the middle gate, entering only when called—as palace officers do.」

sentences.zh: 永明十一年，文惠太子薨，右僕射王晏等奏：「案喪服經『為君之父、長子，同齊衰朞』。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongming, Crown Prince Wenhui died; Right Vice Director Wang Yan and others memorialized: 「According to the Mourning Garments classic, 『For the lord's father and eldest son, the same equated mourning period.』
translations.idiomatic: Yongming 11: Crown Prince Wenhui died. Vice Director Wang Yan and others wrote: 「The Mourning Garments classic says: 『For the lord's father and eldest son, the same equated mourning period.』

sentences.zh: 今至尊既不行三年之典，止服朞制，羣臣應降一等，便應大功。

translations.literal: Now the Supreme Sovereign, since he does not perform the three-year rite, stops at period mourning, the assembled ministers should drop one grade and thus wear greater processed hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Since the sovereign does not observe the full three-year rite but only the one-year mourning, the ministers should drop one grade and wear greater processed hemp.

sentences.zh: 九月功衰，是兄弟之服，不可以服尊。

translations.literal: Nine-month diminished labor is the dress of brothers; one may not wear it for a superior.
translations.idiomatic: Nine-month diminished labor is brothers' mourning; it cannot be worn for a superior.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，謂宜重其衰裳，減其月數，同服齊衰三月。

translations.literal: We your ministers, deliberating together, hold that one should make the sackcloth heavier and reduce the number of months, all wearing dressed sackcloth for three months.
translations.idiomatic: We submit that the sackcloth should be heavier and the months fewer—everyone alike in three months of dressed sackcloth.

sentences.zh: 至於太孫三年既申，南郡國臣，宜備齊衰朞服。

translations.literal: As for the imperial grandson, once his three years are complete, the ministers of the Nankang principality should fully prepare one-year dressed sackcloth.
translations.idiomatic: Once the imperial grandson's three-year term is complete, Nankang's ministers should wear the full one-year dressed sackcloth.

sentences.zh: 臨汝、曲江既非正嫡，不得禰先儲，二公國臣，竝不得服。

translations.literal: Linru and Qujiang, not being legitimate heirs, may not enshrine the former heir designate; the ministers of the two princedoms alike may not wear mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Linru and Qujiang were not legitimate heirs and could not honor the former heir; neither princedom's ministers should mourn.

sentences.zh: 」詔依所議。

translations.literal: 」An edict followed the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: 」The edict approved their proposal.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「案喪服經雖有『妾為君之長子從君而服』，二漢以來，此禮久廢，請因循前准，不復追行。

translations.literal: They memorialized again: 「According to the Mourning Dress Classic, though there is the passage "a concubine, for the lord's eldest son, follows the lord in mourning," since the two Han this rite has long been abandoned; we ask to follow earlier precedent and not revive it.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized again: 「The Mourning Dress Classic does say that a concubine follows the lord in mourning for his eldest son, but since the two Han the rite has been dead; we ask to follow earlier precedent and not revive it.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「既久廢，停便。」

translations.literal: 」The edict said: 「Since it has long been abandoned, let it rest.」
translations.idiomatic: 」The edict read: 「It has been abandoned too long—leave it so.」

sentences.zh: 又奏：「伏尋御服文惠太子朞內不奏樂，諸王雖本服朞，而儲皇正體宗廟，服者一同，釋服，奏樂姻娶，便應竝通。

translations.literal: They memorialized again: 「We reflect that in imperial mourning for Crown Prince Wenhui, within the period no music is performed; though the princes' own mourning is period mourning, the heir designate is the proper body of the ancestral temple—the wearers are one; when mourning is released, music and marriage should likewise be permitted together.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized again: 「In imperial mourning for Crown Prince Wenhui, no music is played during the year; though the princes themselves are in period mourning, the heir is the temple's proper body and the grade is one—when mourning ends, music and marriage should be allowed alike.

sentences.zh: 竊謂二等誠俱是嘉禮，輕重有異。

translations.literal: I submit that both grades are indeed joyous rites, but their weight differs.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that both are joyous rites, but not of the same weight.

sentences.zh: 娶婦思嗣，事非全吉，三日不樂，禮有明文。

translations.literal: Taking a wife to think of heirs is not wholly auspicious; three days without music—the rites have explicit text.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage to secure an heir is not wholly auspicious; three days without music—the rites say so plainly.

sentences.zh: 宋世朞喪降在大功者，婚禮廢樂，以申私戚，通以前典。

translations.literal: In Song, those whose period mourning was reduced to greater processed hemp still suspended music at weddings, to express private grief—this accords with earlier precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song, mourners reduced from the year to greater processed hemp still laid music aside at weddings to show private grief—following older precedent.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「案禮，祥除皆先於今夕易服，明旦乃設祭。

translations.literal: They memorialized again: 「According to the rites, at the end of xiang mourning one always changes dress this evening, and only at dawn sets out the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized again: 「By the rites, the end of xiang mourning always means changing dress the night before and holding the sacrifice only at dawn.

sentences.zh: 尋比世服臨然後改服，與禮為乖。

translations.literal: Examining recent ages, they wear mourning at the visit and only then change dress—this departs from the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In recent practice men still wear mourning at the visit and change only afterward—that departs from the rites.

sentences.zh: 今東宮公除日，若依例皇太孫服臨方易服。

translations.literal: On the Eastern Palace's day of public mourning release, if one follows precedent the imperial grandson should change dress only at the mourning visit.
translations.idiomatic: On the Eastern Palace's public release day, precedent would have the imperial grandson change dress only at the mourning visit.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，謂先哭臨竟而後祭之。

translations.literal: We your ministers, deliberating together, hold that one should weep at the visit to its end and only then sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: We submit that one should finish weeping at the visit first and only then offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 應公除者，皆於府第變服，而後入臨，行奉慰之禮。

translations.literal: All who owe public release should change dress at their residence first, then enter the visit and perform the condolence rite.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone due for public release should change dress at home, then enter the visit and perform the condolence rite.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，朝會，時世祖遏密未終，朝議疑作樂不？

translations.literal: Jianwu 2, at court assembly—the Shizu emperor's mourning taboo was not yet ended, and court debate doubted whether to perform music.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 2, at court assembly, Emperor Shizu's mourning taboo was not yet over, and the court debated whether music should be played.

sentences.zh: 祠部郎何佟之議：「昔舜受終文祖，義非胤堯，及放勛徂落，遏密三祀。

translations.literal: He Tongzhi of the Directorate of Sacrifices argued: 「In antiquity Shun received the mandate from Wenzu; in principle he did not inherit Yao; when Fangxun passed away, he suppressed music for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He Tongzhi, directorate-of-sacrifices attendant, argued: 「When Shun received the mandate from Wenzu he did not, in principle, inherit Yao; when Fangxun died, he suppressed music for three years.

sentences.zh: 近代晉康帝繼成帝，于時亦不作樂。

translations.literal: In recent times Jin Emperor Kang succeeded Emperor Cheng; at that time likewise no music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, Emperor Kang succeeded Emperor Cheng and likewise made no music.

sentences.zh: 懷帝永嘉元年，惠帝喪制未終，于時江充議云，古帝王相承，雖世及有異，而輕重同禮。

translations.literal: In Yongjia 1 of Emperor Huai, Emperor Hui's mourning was not yet ended; at that time Jiang Chong argued that from antiquity successive emperors, though succession differed, shared the same rites in weight.
translations.idiomatic: In Huai's Yongjia 1, while Emperor Hui's mourning was unfinished, Jiang Chong held that successive rulers, though succession differed, observed the same rites in weight.

sentences.zh: 〔宗〕文皇帝今二年正月二十四日再忌日，二十九日大祥，三月二十九日祥禫，至尊及羣臣泄哀之儀，應定准。

translations.literal: [Zong] Emperor Wen: in the second year, the twenty-fourth day of the first month is the second death anniversary, the twenty-ninth is major xiang, the twenty-ninth of the third month is xiang removal; the rites for the sovereign and assembled ministers to pour forth grief should be fixed by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen (temple name Shizong): in the second year, the twenty-fourth day of the first month is the second death anniversary; the twenty-ninth is major xiang; the twenty-ninth of the third month is xiang removal. sentences.zh: 下二學八座丞郎。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the two academies, the eight seats, directors, and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was circulated to the two academies, the eight seats, and the directorate and attendant ranks.

sentences.zh: 博士陶韶以為「名立義生，自古之制。

translations.literal: Erudite Tao Shao held that 「when the name is established the duty arises—this is the regulation from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Tao Shao held: 「When the title is fixed the obligation follows—that is ancient regulation.

sentences.zh: 文帝正號祖宗，式序昭穆，祥忌禫日，皇帝宜服祭服，出太極泄哀，百僚亦祭服陪位」。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen has the proper title among ancestors and founders, ordering the zhao and mu; on xiang, death-day, and removal days the emperor should wear sacrificial dress, go out from the Supreme Ultimate to pour forth grief, and the hundred offices should also attend in sacrificial dress.」
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen now stands properly among ancestors; on xiang, memorial, and removal days the emperor should wear sacrificial robes, leave the Supreme Ultimate hall to pour forth grief, and the hundred offices should attend in sacrificial dress likewise.」

sentences.zh: 太常丞李撝議曰：「尋尊號既追，重服宜正，但已從權制，故苴杖不說。

translations.literal: Aide Li Huo of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials argued: 「Examining the matter, once the honorific title was granted, full mourning should be correct; but having already followed expedient regulation, the hemp staff is not mentioned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huo, aide in the chamberlainate for ceremonials, argued: 「Once the posthumous title was granted, full mourning would be proper; but the court already followed an expedient rule, so the hemp staff is not discussed.

sentences.zh: 至於鑽燧既同，天地亦變，容得無感乎。

translations.literal: Yet when fire-sticks are alike, Heaven and Earth also change—can one be without feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the fire-drill is the same, Heaven and Earth change too—how could one feel nothing?

sentences.zh: 且晉景獻皇后崩，羣臣備小君之服。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Jin's Jingxian empress died, the assembled ministers prepared the dress for a lesser mistress.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's Jingxian empress died, the ministers wore the dress owed a lesser mistress.

sentences.zh: 追尊之后，無違后典，追尊之帝，固宜同帝禮矣。

translations.literal: After posthumous elevation to empress, one does not violate empress precedent; a posthumously elevated emperor should likewise follow emperor rites.
translations.idiomatic: After posthumous elevation to empress there is no breach of empress precedent; a posthumously elevated emperor should follow emperor rites all the more.

sentences.zh: 雖臣子一例，而禮隨時異，至尊龍飛中興，事非嗣武，理無深衣之變。

translations.literal: Though ministers and sons share one rule, rites vary with the times; the Supreme Sovereign's dragon flight at restoration is not succession like continuing Wu—there is no reason for a change to deep garments.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers and sons may share one rule, but rites shift with the age; the sovereign's restoration is not succession in the manner of continuing Wu—there is no call for deep-garment mourning.

sentences.zh: 但王者體國，亦應弔服出正殿舉哀，百寮致慟，一如常儀。

translations.literal: Yet the king embodies the state; he should also wear condolence dress, go out to the main hall to lament, and the hundred offices express grief—just as in the usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the king embodies the state: he should wear condolence dress, go out to the main hall to lament, and the hundred offices express grief as in ordinary rites.

translations.literal: [Tan] Ji argued: 「Mourning rites are one system, but the limits split in two.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tanji argued: 「Mourning is one system, but its limits divide in two.

sentences.zh: 虞祔追亡之情，小祥抑存之禮，斯蓋至愛可申，極痛宜屈耳。

translations.literal: The feeling of yu and fu pursues the dead; the rite of minor xiang restrains remembrance of the living—this is where utmost love may extend and utmost pain should bend.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and fu pursue the dead; minor xiang restrains remembrance of the living—there utmost love may extend and utmost pain should yield.

sentences.zh: 文皇帝雖君德早凝，民化未洽，追崇尊極，寔緣于性。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, though his lordly virtue was early set, the people's transformation was not yet complete, yet posthumous exaltation to the utmost sprang from nature.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen's virtue was early formed though the people were not yet fully transformed; posthumous exaltation sprang from nature alone.

sentences.zh: 今言臣則無實，論己則事虛。

translations.literal: Speaking now as a minister lacks substance; speaking of oneself the matter is empty.
translations.idiomatic: As ministers we have no real standing here; for ourselves the matter is hollow.

sentences.zh: 聖上馭㝢，更奉天眷，祗禮七廟，非從三后，周忌祥禫，無所依設。

translations.literal: The sage sovereign rules the realm, again receives Heaven's favor, reverently serves the seven temples—not following three empresses; the cycle of memorial, xiang, and removal has nothing on which to be set.
translations.idiomatic: The sage sovereign rules the realm under Heaven's renewed favor, reverently tends the seven temples—not as heir to three empresses—so the cycle of memorial, xiang, and removal has no footing.

translations.literal: He Tongzhi of the Directorate of Sacrifices argued: 「The intent of the Spring and Autumn is that ministers and sons succeed lords and parents; though favor and obligation differ, the rites are one—thereby to deepen the feeling of nourishing respect and make firm the meaning of square mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He Tongzhi argued: 「The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that ministers and sons succeed lords and parents; obligations differ, but the rites are one—to deepen nourishing respect and firm the meaning of proper mourning.

sentences.zh: 主上雖仰嗣高皇，嘗經北面，方今聖曆御宇，垂訓無窮，在三之恩，理不容替。

translations.literal: Though the sovereign succeeded Gaohuang and once faced north to him, now the sage reign governs the realm and his teachings are endless—the threefold obligation cannot, in principle, be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Though the sovereign succeeded Gaohuang and once faced north to him, the sage reign now governs without end—the threefold obligation cannot be set aside.

translations.literal: 〔宗〕On xiang taboo days, the Supreme Sovereign should wear condolence dress and ascend the hall; the assembled ministers should alike express mournful feeling; when the rite is complete, the hundred officials should go to Xuande Palace to present a memorial, and still extend grief at the imperial tomb, to magnify longing for the distant dead.

translations.literal: When the Prince of Hailing died, the hundred officials gathered for mourning; at that time the court was in strict assembly order, and court debate doubted whether to attend in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince of Hailing died, officials gathered to mourn; the court was under strict assembly rules, and men debated whether to appear in military dress.

sentences.zh: 祠部郎何佟之議：「羔裘玄冠不以弔。

translations.idiomatic: He Tongzhi of the sacrifices directorate argued: 「Lamb-fur robe and black cap are not for condolence calls.

translations.literal: In principle one cannot attend a funeral in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: In principle one cannot stand at a funeral in arms.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始二年，孝武大祥之日，于時百寮入臨，皆於宮門變戎服，著衣𢂿，入臨畢出外，還襲戎衣。

sentences.zh: 贊曰：姬制孔作，訓範百王。

translations.literal: Appraisal: Zhou's institutions, Confucius wrought—models for a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Zhou laid the pattern; Confucius gave it form—a model for a hundred kings.

sentences.zh: 三千有數，四維是張。

translations.literal: Three thousand rules have their measure; the four bonds are spread wide.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand rites keep their count; the four bonds stretch taut across the realm.

sentences.zh: 損益彜典，廢舉憲章。

translations.literal: The canonical Yi is adjusted and reduced; constitutional statutes are abolished and raised.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi canon is trimmed and enlarged; statutes are cast down and raised again.

sentences.zh: 戎祀軍國，社廟郊庠。

translations.literal: Military rites and state sacrifice; altars of soil and grain, suburban rites, and the school.
translations.idiomatic: Army rites and state sacrifice; soil-altars and grain-halls, suburban worship, royal school.

sentences.zh: 冠婚朝會，服紀凶喪。

translations.literal: Caps and marriage, court assemblies; garment codes for misfortune and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Capping and wedding, court and assembly; dress and rule for grief and the dead.

sentences.zh: 存為盛德，戒在先亡。

translations.literal: What is preserved becomes great virtue; the warning lies in what perished before.
translations.idiomatic: What endures is great virtue; the warning is written in what died first.
